implementerProof.how: Round 6: I reproduced the defect behind each of its two code fixes rather than reading its negative controls — reverting both providers conditions fails exactly the two cloudsql-iam subtests and no others, and I then drove the fix's consequence on the real `legion worker-shim` binary, which its own proof does not do. Its exporter claim I drove to `collect_transcripts`'s return code and read the two lines that turn that into a run failure. Its sweep claims I re-derived. Rounds 1 to 5 were each verified as those rounds record.

proof.criterion: A deployment on the second database kind must be able to boot: the shim and the image probe are told the providers directory only where the pod mounts it.
proof.surface: The sandbox package's rig for the rule, driven as a defect reproduction in an out-of-tree copy; and the **real `legion worker-shim` binary** for the consequence, which is where the defect would have been met.
proof.command: Revert both `if r.mountsProviders()` conditions (launcher.go's shim argv, probe.go's probe command) and run `go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox -run TestTheProvidersDirectoryIsToldWhereThePodMountsIt -v`; restore and re-run. Then `legion worker-shim --connect unix:///nonexistent.sock --boot-token-file <file> --provider-env-dir <a directory that does not exist> -- /bin/true`, and the same command without the flag.
proof.observed: Unfixed, exactly the two `cloudsql-iam with no provider key` subtests fail — a role's shim and the image probe, each showing `--provider-env-dir /var/run/legion/providers` in the argv with `want false` — while `cloudsql-iam with a provider key` and `postgres with no provider key` pass unchanged. Restored, all pass. On the real binary the consequence is immediate: `legion worker-shim: --provider-env-dir … is unreadable: open …: no such file or directory`, **exit 1 before it dials the daemon**. So under `cloudsql-iam` with no provider key every role's shim would have exited 1 at every launch and the deployment could not have booted.
proof.negativeControl: The same shim command with no `--provider-env-dir` proceeds to dialling and retries the daemon stream (exit 141 on my timeout), so the refusal is the directory's and not a missing socket, a missing token file or a bad argv.

proof.criterion: The hardened exporter's refusals fail the run, and both halves of a colliding pair are refused rather than the first one winning.
proof.surface: The real `collect_transcripts` and `session_copy` functions extracted from `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh` and run with only their database call stubbed, on the hex listing a real PostgreSQL produced in round 5.
proof.command: `collect_transcripts` with a failing and a succeeding `session_copy`; then `session_copy` over the round-5 listing, which holds a colliding pair, with the output directory walked afterwards
proof.observed: `collect_transcripts` returns 1 when the copy refuses a key and 0 otherwise. The teardown turns that into `CHECK transcripts: FAIL` and a non-empty `teardown_failed`, which prints `stage 4b e2e: FAIL` (read at `:2584-2586` and `:2626-2627`; the return code is driven, those two lines are read). The colliding pair is refused in **both** directions: each key is named and names the other, `exit=1`, and the three good keys are still copied — `sub.jsonl`, `.._escape.jsonl`, `__n__code.jsonl`.
proof.negativeControl: What distinguishes this from first-come, which a single collision would otherwise look identical to: `\n` (0x0a) sorts before `/` (0x2f), so the listing hands the newline key to the loop first and a first-come rule would have written `a_b.jsonl` from it. That file is absent.

Nothing asserts a Sandbox-owned issue volume or one outliving its pod; the only matching hit is `live_lifecycle_test.go:563`, which asserts the **absence** of such a claim. All six reference sites are closed: no `only store` in the example file, the site page, `scripts/e2e/README.md` or `AGENTS.md`; no `must be postgres` or `must name session_store: postgres` in the site page; no `SessionDSNKey` in `names.go`.

Each is true of the pod's own disk and asserts nothing the change removed, so the class is closed in the sense asked and these are vocabulary, not model. I say so rather than report the class clean and leave four hits for the next reader to re-derive.

bodySize: The pull request body reached 64,125 of GitHub's 65,536 characters this round, at which point an edit is refused outright and the body stops being editable by anyone, including the merger. I moved rounds 1 to 3 of the tester block into a comment verbatim (linked above) and left a pointer, which returned it to 48,506. Nothing was lost: a comment outlives retro's removal of `.legion/`, where the handoff does not.
residualRisks: Unchanged from round 5: the single generation counter behind the gap record; a daemon restarting inside the replacement's gap; and the stable claim name meaning a replacement pod waits on its predecessor's claim being reaped, about a second against a 120 s boot timeout.

The exporter copies what it can and fails the run, so a refused key leaves a run that failed with most evidence kept rather than a run that passed with evidence missing. That is the right trade and it is worth knowing that the two states look alike in the directory and differ only in the verdict line.
